subject: Food Science
title: Salt as the First Preservative
description: A fast breakdown of Salt as the First Preservative for builders.

hook.text: Roman soldiers were partly paid in salt—the word 'salary' comes from 'salarium.' Salt was that valuable because it preserved food.

buildup.text: Salt preserves by drawing water out of food through osmosis. Bacteria can't survive in the resulting low-moisture environment.

discovery.text: Salt as the First Preservative reveals the mechanism or argument that changes the picture.

twist.text: Salt wars shaped geopolitics for centuries. Trade routes, taxes, and monopolies on salt caused revolutions.

climax.text: Industrial salt production in the 1800s made salt cheap and abundant. It shifted from luxury preservative to everyday commodity.

punchline.text: A crystal that drew out water and stopped rot.

quiz.question: Where does the word 'salary' come from?
options: Latin 'salarium'—because Roman soldiers were partly paid in salt
